seo.meta_title: What Does 빼먹다 Mean? | Not 'Take Out and Eat'
seo.meta_description: AI glosses 빼먹다 as 'take out and eat'. It means leaving something out by mistake, or skipping class or work. What to say to your boss instead.

ai_failure.situation: Your team leader checks your report and says: 여기 한 줄 빼먹었네요.
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Glosses it as 'You took out and ate one line here.'
ai_failure.why_it_fails: 빼먹다 means leaving something out by mistake, or skipping something on purpose (수업을 빼먹다, 'cut class'). Nothing is eaten. Your leader is pointing out a missing line.

natural_solution.rule: 빼먹다 = miss or skip. It's casual. About your own mistake at work, 빠뜨렸습니다 or 누락했습니다 sounds more professional.

alternatives.context: To your boss: 'Sorry, I missed it. I'll fix it right away.'
Casual, to yourself or friends: 'I forgot one!'
'I skipped class today' — sounds like playing hooky, not an excused absence

nuance: 빼먹다 comes from 빼다 ('take out') + 먹다, but it has nothing to do with eating. Because it can mean skipping on purpose, don't use it for a real absence when talking to your boss: 회사를 빼먹었어요 sounds like you skipped work for fun. For a real absence, say 결근했어요 or 쉬었어요.
